uncertainty: Five C JSON third-party paths pass two valid controls with format-aware tree results, parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback. The original Conan recipe search missed Debian-packaged C parsers; a bounded Debian source-name search for 'json' (320 hits) plus exact lookups for jansson, jq, frozen, jsmn and parson in the same hashed popcon snapshot found the Debian-packaged C parser leads. libfastjson is a json-c fork and shares the json-c tokener family; jq's count is the jq source package (mostly the command-line program), and its jv C API is documented on the project wiki without a stability commitment; jq numbers have one kind, so integer/float in its tree comes from the preserved decimal literal. frozen fails the nested-object control (\u00e9 decoded to one Latin-1 byte), jsmn is tokenizer-only, and liblaxjson (1 installation) and parson (no Debian source) remain unselected. Debian installations mostly reflect dependencies and miss vendored copies. These paths do not establish a definitive top ten or full RFC 8259 compliance. ISO C documents no JSON API.
selection: Five control-verified C JSON packages rank by Debian popcon sourcemax installations from one hashed snapshot: jansson 2.15.1 (282,984), json-c 0.19 (269,736), json-glib 1.10.8 (163,249), cjson 1.7.19 (150,958), yyjson 0.13.0 (14,868).
